title: AI in the Real World
description: Explore how AI systems are deployed across industries—search, healthcare, finance, transportation, and creative work.
learningObjectives: Explain how AI systems improve over time
Recognize ethical considerations in AI deployment

content.content: AI has moved from labs into nearly every industry. Search engines, hospitals, banks, and transportation systems all use AI as core infrastructure.
Healthcare: AI detects tumors in X-rays. Finance: AI detects fraud in real-time. Transportation: AI powers route optimization and self-driving systems.

sections.title: How AI Systems Learn and Improve

content.content: Modern AI systems improve through feedback loops. Every user interaction generates data, which is used to refine the model.
This is why AI products can feel like they 'get better' over time: the system is learning from millions of users every day.
Feedback Loop: The cycle where AI output leads to user behavior, which generates data, which refines the AI.
AI systems can amplify bias present in their training data. Facial recognition, hiring algorithms, and loan decisions have all shown racial or gender bias.
Responsible AI is not just a technical challenge—it's a governance and design challenge. Understanding who is affected by AI decisions matters as much as the model itself.

flashcards.front: Name three industries using AI as core infrastructure.
flashcards.back: Healthcare, finance, transportation (also: search, education, media).

flashcards.front: What is a feedback loop in AI?
flashcards.back: A cycle where AI output affects user behavior, generating data that refines the AI.

flashcards.front: Why can AI systems amplify bias?
flashcards.back: Because training data may contain bias, and AI learns from that data.

items.question: Why do AI products tend to improve over time?
options: Because they learn from user data through feedback loops
items.explanation: AI systems improve by learning from data generated by user interactions.

items.question: Why is ethical AI important?
items.answer: Because AI systems can amplify bias, affect lives through decisions, and require governance—not just technical solutions.
items.explanation: AI affects real people. Responsible design and governance are essential.

notes.summary: AI is deployed across industries and improves through feedback loops, raising significant ethical considerations.
